A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Density-Aware Farthest Point Sampling by the same authors. The main text, equations, nine figures, and appendices A–N are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression experiments, computational timings, data analyses, and hyperparameter ablations in Section 8 and Appendices F–M.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including molecular and non-molecular regression benchmarks, timing measurements, and ZINC ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the density estimators, adaptive neighborhood weights, and selection objective remain unchanged. The expanded discussion of hyperparameters and weighting choices does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM7, QM8, QM9, ZINC, Concrete Compressive Strength, Electrical Grid Stability, and the synthetic 2D illustration. Their prediction tasks and test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain RDM, FPS, facility location, and k-medoids++. Appendix K retains Twinning and Gaussian facility location, while Appendices L–M retain the same FPS-initialized comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training-set budgets, preprocessing, regression models, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation on unselected pool points are unchanged. Both versions retain MAE, RMSE, and MAXAE evaluations and Appendix K’s distinct training-size ratios.

E4.justification: The data-assumption analysis, FPS-initialization comparisons, ZINC sensitivity studies for u and k, and Gaussian facility-location tuning analysis are already present in v1 and retained in v2. Expanded explanations add no new analytical experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report predictive-result standard deviations over five runs and retain the same repeat and initialization information. No run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: Figures 1–9 retain the same plotted results and findings. Appendix F’s timings, including QM9’s 1,974-second NumPy and 968-second PyTorch measurements, and Appendix H’s correlation coefficients are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 tightens the existing bound by multiplying the combined label-uncertainty and training-error term by the newly defined probability P_L[p_XD < p_XL]. Appendix C revises the derivation accordingly. This is a bounded refinement: the assumptions, density-estimation results, and DA-FPS approximation theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a weighted-fill-distance error bound, the passive model-agnostic DA-FPS algorithm, approximation guarantees, and improved average prediction performance. The theorem refinement does not redefine these overarching claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretation of the distribution-mismatch factor and zero weighted fill distance, explains k-related variance and smoothing tradeoffs, and justifies multiplicative weighting. It also makes the u = 0 guarantee versus u > 0 practical initialization distinction explicit and expands the existing discussion of unreliable density estimates.

D1.justification: Section 8 newly provides a GitHub repository link for reproducing its results; v1 contains no corresponding code-access link. Existing preprocessing, hardware, implementation, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference list are unchanged. Referring to Climaco and Garcke (2024) as the authors’ earlier work preserves the existing relationship and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a paper roadmap, section-opening summaries, expanded explanations, acknowledgments, and author-information updates, alongside language corrections. These additions preserve the overall section sequence, appendix organization, and most existing prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 summarizing notation. Existing figures retain their panels and plotted content, with adjustments to sizing, spacing, and placement, including moving Figure 7 above its surrounding discussion.

improvement.justification: v2 tightens Theorem 4.2 and its proof, clarifies the limits of the approximation guarantee and density estimation, and adds useful notation and reproducibility information. These changes improve precision and usability while retaining the method and empirical evidence. The unresolved connection between the estimated and true weighted fill distances remains.
